strategy_prompt: Use the provided image as the reference. Produce a NEW, original image of the same subject (the product). Keep the product itself EXACTLY the same — identical shape, colour, materials, proportions, branding, logos and any printed text. Match the visual style and MEDIUM of the reference: if it is a photograph keep it photographic; if it is illustrated, cartoon or animated, keep that exact style and do NOT make it photorealistic. Refresh the specific background details and change the camera angle so it reads as a new, original shot rather than a copy — but keep the change moderate and do not invent an unrelated scene. Keep the SAME TYPE of setting as the reference (originally: A stylized bathroom setting, featuring a mirror, sink, and a towel on a rack): you may vary the specific decor, props, colours and layout for originality, but the scene must stay the same kind of place — a kitchen stays a kitchen, a bedroom stays a bedroom, a bathroom stays a bathroom, an outdoor shot stays outdoors. Preserve the composition and action: keep a person holding (showing the face and hand), in the same pose and framing, and preserve EXACTLY the product or demonstrated effect shown on them (e.g. the makeup / lash / skin result). BUT for originality the person MUST be a DIFFERENT individual from the reference — recreate a similar-looking person (same gender, approximate age, hair colour, skin tone and overall style) but with a clearly different face and identity. Never reproduce the real person shown in the reference. Keep the product the clear main focus. Any overlaid marketing caption from the reference may be removed. Output aspect ratio 3:4.
